title: Two Sum
prompt:
Read a line of space-separated integers, then a second line with a single integer `target`. Exactly two of the numbers add up to `target`; print their indices (0-based, ascending) separated by a space.

Input:
  2 7 11 15
  9
Output:
  0 1
spoken_intro: Let's start with a short coding exercise. You'll read a list of numbers and a target, and print the indices of the two numbers that add up to it. Run it against the test cases, and submit when you're happy.

spoken_intro: Here's an easy warm-up. Read a line of text and print it reversed. Try the test cases and submit when ready.

title: FizzBuzz
prompt: Print the numbers from 1 to 15, one per line. For multiples of 3 print "Fizz", for multiples of 5 print "Buzz", and for multiples of both print "FizzBuzz". No input is given.
spoken_intro: Let's do FizzBuzz. Print one through fifteen, replacing multiples of three with Fizz, five with Buzz, and both with FizzBuzz. Run the test and submit when ready.

title: Count Vowels
prompt:
Read a single line of text and print how many vowels (a, e, i, o, u) it contains, case-insensitive.

Input:
  Interview
Output:
  4
spoken_intro: A quick string problem. Read a line of text and print how many vowels it has, ignoring case. Test it and submit when ready.

title: Maximum in a List
prompt:
Read a line of space-separated integers and print the largest one. Do not use your language's built-in max function.

Input:
  3 7 2 9 4
Output:
  9
spoken_intro: Here's a simple one. Read a list of integers and print the largest, without using the built-in max function. Run the tests and submit when you're done.
